chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan said:

I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for several days; he would recite 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' in the Opening of the Book. When it was a prayer in which recitation was not pronounced aloud, he would pronounce 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' aloud and keep silent (conceal) everything else.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)
key_terms.لَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ: In which recitation is not pronounced aloud (silent prayer)

ai.seo_question: How should the Basmala be recited at the beginning of Al-Fatiha in silent versus audible prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical application of the Basmala in Salah, specifically noting Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) method of reciting it aloud in *Jahri* prayers and silently in *Sutri* prayers. This ruling underscores the scholarly consensus on the Basmala as an integral part of Surah Al-Fatiha rather than a separate verse, influencing the distinction between audible and silent recitation in Shia jurisprudence. It reflects the meticulous attention to ritual precision (*adab*) in the Imams' worship, serving as a primary evidence for the permissibility and preference of reciting the Basmala within the Fatiha during daily prayers.
